project.name: libfdk-aac
project.fixed_commit_note: The staged fix is source-relevant: it changes `sbrDecoder_Header()` so a failed external SBR-header update forces `hSbrHeader->syncState = SBR_NOT_INITIALIZED; hSbrHeader->status = HEADER_ERROR;`. Stage 01 did not save a fixed-build rerun, and `runtime_disambiguation` is disabled, so this role treats the patch as supporting source evidence rather than as dynamically confirmed remediation for the reproduced UBSan crash.

analysis_state.reason: Stage 01 reproduced the UBSan index-out-of-bounds write in `sbrGetChannelElement()`. The vulnerable source closes two local facts: `resetFreqBandTables()` can store an oversized `freqBandData.nInvfBands` into a rejected external-header slot, and the crashing call later uses a live header whose `nInvfBands` exceeds 5 and overruns `sbr_invf_mode[5]`. What the saved artifacts do not disambiguate, because `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, is whether `sbrDecoder_Parse()` reached the sink with that rejected slot still selected or with a full `copySbrHeader()` from `lastHdrSlot`.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where SBR data is not discarded in the case of an unsuccessful SBR header update, potentially leading to incorrect processing or use of invalid data.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `runtime error: index 5 out of bounds for type 'INVF_MODE [5]'` at `libSBRdec/src/env_extr.cpp:763`. In vulnerable source, external SBR-header parsing reads attacker-controlled header fields, `resetFreqBandTables()` derives a concrete noise-band count from them, and line 817 copies that count into persistent `freqBandData.nInvfBands` before line 819 rejects counts above `MAX_NOISE_COEFFS` (5). The later sink-side loop uses the selected header's `nInvfBands` as its bound and UBSan proves that runtime bound exceeds 5. The fix patch hardens one specific reuse path by invalidating failed external-header slots in `sbrDecoder_Header()`. The saved Stage 01 artifacts, however, do not independently record whether `sbrdecoder.cpp:1249-1256` reached the crash with the rejected slot still live or with `copySbrHeader()` copying another slot into place.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed path that materializes attacker-controlled external SBR-header bits into persistent decoder header state.
source.value_from: The staged 134-byte witness is fed to the LOAS decoder opened by `aacDecoder_Open(TT_MP4_LOAS, ...)`. When the project parses an external SBR header, this line reads attacker-controlled bits from `hBs` into `hHeaderData->bs_data` and `hHeaderData->bs_info`. The saved artifacts do not disambiguate which external-header occurrence later supplied the crashing slot state.

tainted_value_origin.description: Exact source-level producer of an oversized candidate inverse-filter loop limit in the rejected external-header state. The attacker-derived noise-band count is copied into persistent `freqBandData.nInvfBands` before the following guard rejects counts above 5.

root_cause.description: The decoder writes an oversized inverse-filter loop bound into persistent header state before proving that the same count fits the 5-entry inverse-filter arrays later used if that header state remains live.
root_cause.note: The staged fix does not move this store. Instead, it invalidates failed external-header slots later in `sbrDecoder_Header()` so a rejected header cannot remain live. Because Stage 01 did not record which slot/status arm at `sbrdecoder.cpp:1249-1256` supplied the sink-side `hSbrHeader`, this step remains the strongest source-grounded producer, not a closed sink-reaching data edge.

sink.description: UBSan crash site. The first invalid loop iteration writes index 5 into the fixed-size `sbr_invf_mode[5]` array.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `runtime error: index 5 out of bounds for type 'INVF_MODE [5]'` at this exact statement, with stack `sbrGetChannelElement -> sbrDecoder_Parse -> aacDecoder_ParseExplicitMpsAndSbr -> CAacDecoder_DecodeFrame`.

parser_admitted.description: The saved UBSan stack proves the witness reaches explicit SBR parsing and calls `sbrDecoder_Parse()` on the crashing path.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 may not instrument the ARVO workspace to observe which branch at `sbrdecoder.cpp:1249-1256` fired in the crashing run.

The saved artifacts prove the sink-side fact `nInvfBands > 5` because UBSan reports the first invalid write at index 5 on type `INVF_MODE [5]`. They do not record whether `sbrDecoder_Parse()` reached that loop by keeping the current slot under `SBRDEC_HDR_STAT_UPDATE` or by `copySbrHeader()` from `lastHdrSlot`, and `copySbrHeader()` clones the whole `SBR_HEADER_DATA` including `freqBandData`.
Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable build. There is no saved fixed-build rerun for this sample, so `patch_resolves` remains false here even though the patch is source-relevant.

coarse_trace.summary: External SBR-header parsing reads attacker-controlled header fields and reports that the header requires a reset.
Frequency-table recomputation derives an oversized noise-band count, copies it into persistent `nInvfBands`, and only then rejects the header as unsupported.
The external-header failure path leaves slot liveness bookkeeping untouched; the fix patch hardens this point by forcing `syncState = SBR_NOT_INITIALIZED` and `status = HEADER_ERROR`.

Later parse-time slot selection uses `getHeaderSlot()` plus the `SBRDEC_HDR_STAT_UPDATE` / `copySbrHeader()` logic to decide whether the current free slot is kept or overwritten; Stage 01 does not record which arm preserved the crashing header.
The inverse-filter loop trusts the selected header's `nInvfBands`; UBSan proves the crashing bound exceeds the 5-entry array, but the saved artifacts do not identify which earlier slot supplied it.

fine_trace.note: Source. The external SBR-header parser consumes attacker-controlled bits from `hBs` and writes them into persistent header fields `bs_data` and `bs_info`, including `startFreq`, `stopFreq`, `xover_band`, and `noise_bands`.

Because the parsed header differs from the previously active header state or arrives before SBR is initialized, `sbrGetHeaderData()` returns `HEADER_RESET` and sends the header through `sbrDecoder_HeaderUpdate()` and `resetFreqBandTables()`.

During frequency-table reset, the parsed frequency-range fields and `noise_bands` are converted into a concrete noise-band count `nNfb`. On the witnessed path this count exceeds `MAX_NOISE_COEFFS` (5), which is corroborated by the later first invalid loop index `i == 5` on a 5-entry destination array.

Root-cause value producer. Before any rejection happens, the oversized `nNfb` is copied into persistent `freqBandData.nInvfBands` inside the current header slot, creating an oversized candidate loop bound if that slot later survives reuse.
Only after step 4 stores the loop bound does the decoder detect that the count is unsupported and return `SBRDEC_UNSUPPORTED_CONFIG`.

The vulnerable external-header failure path has no `else` branch. When step 5 returns an error, the slot is not forced to `SBR_NOT_INITIALIZED` and its `status` is not reset to `HEADER_ERROR`. The fix patch adds exactly that invalidation.

With `self->numDelayFrames = 1`, the decoder manages two header slots. Parse derives `lastHdrSlot` from the previously used frame slot, computes `thisHdrSlot` as the free slot via `getHeaderSlot()`, and binds `hSbrHeader` to that free slot for the current frame.

This block is the unresolved slot bridge between the rejected external-header state and the later sink. If `status & SBRDEC_HDR_STAT_UPDATE` is still set, parse keeps the current free slot and just clears the bit. Otherwise, because there are two slots and `thisHdrSlot != lastHdrSlot`, it overwrites the free slot from `lastHdrSlot` with `copySbrHeader()`, which clones the whole `SBR_HEADER_DATA`. `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation, so Stage 01 does not reveal which arm produced the `hSbrHeader` consumed at the crash.

The saved UBSan stack proves the runtime reaches this call site and enters `sbrGetChannelElement()` from `sbrDecoder_Parse()`. The `hSbrHeader` passed here is live SBR state, but the saved artifacts do not disclose whether it is the rejected external-header slot from steps 1-6 or a full copy from `lastHdrSlot` made at step 8.

Sink-side bound observation. The selected header object's `nInvfBands` controls the inverse-filter loop. UBSan's first invalid write at index 5 proves this runtime `nInvfBands` exceeded `MAX_INVF_BANDS` (5), but the saved artifacts do not show whether that value came from the rejected slot produced at step 4 or from a `copySbrHeader()` copy of `lastHdrSlot`.

Sink. On the first invalid iteration, the next 2-bit inverse-filter value is written into `sbr_invf_mode[5]`, one element past the valid `0..4` range. The saved sanitizer trace reports `runtime error: index 5 out of bounds for type 'INVF_MODE [5]'` at this statement; that runtime fact proves the step-10 loop bound exceeded 5 without resolving which earlier slot supplied it.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes for the runtime suffix `aacDecoder_ParseExplicitMpsAndSbr -> sbrDecoder_Parse -> sbrGetChannelElement`. The unresolved part is the earlier header-slot/status history because Stage 01 did not record it and runtime disambiguation is disabled.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Partially. Steps 1-6 prove a rejected external-header state with oversized `nInvfBands`, and steps 9-11 prove the crashing call used a live header whose `nInvfBands` exceeded 5. The saved artifacts do not identify whether `sbrDecoder_Parse()` reached the sink with that same slot or with a `copySbrHeader()` copy from `lastHdrSlot`.

format.name: LOAS AAC/SBR witness
format.contract: The exact 134-byte witness must drive explicit SBR parsing to `sbrGetChannelElement()` and make `hHeaderData->freqBandData.nInvfBands` large enough that the inverse-filter loop reaches `i == 5` on `INVF_MODE sbr_invf_mode[5]`. The saved artifacts do not disambiguate which earlier external-header slot/status transition made that oversize loop bound live.
